Traceability¶

Traceability is being able to answer, for any unit, what was tested, when, where, how, and with what result. For example, a unit comes back from the field: which tests did it pass, which firmware was loaded, which lot was it built in, and which version of the test was used?

Prism records some of this for you. The rest your scripts and test code must record. Plan it before production starts, because results that were not recorded can’t be added later.

Recorded Automatically¶

Every result has these fields in the Lente record table (see Database),

  • ruid, a unique id for this result

  • info_product, info_bom, info_lot, info_location and info_config, from the script info section, often filled in from subs or a Traveller

  • meta_script, the path of the script that ran, for example public/prism/scripts/mycompany/P001/P00100_T0100_SmokeTests.scr

  • meta_git_public, the version of your scripts repo (public/VERSION), see Create a Tag

  • meta_git_prism, the version of Prism

  • meta_uuid_getnode, an id of the Prism computer, derived from its network interface

  • meta_channel, the test channel (jig) that ran the test

  • meta_result, meta_start, meta_end and _duration

Each test item and measurement is stored with its full name, which includes the module path and the item id, for example mycompany.P001.P00100_T0100_SmokeTests.TST0200_measVDD.vdd.

The result JSON file also has the operator and the station IP address. These are kept in the result file backups (public/result/…/bkup), but they are not database columns.

Because meta_git_public is recorded, every file in your scripts repo is traceable: scripts, test code, limits, and firmware images stored with the scripts (for example in an assets folder). Use the version to find the exact files with git checkout.

What You Record¶

Serial Numbers and Unit Ids¶

Save the unit’s serial number (or other unique id) in key0. The Lente Throughput & Yield chart uses product + key0 to count each unit once,

ctx.record.add_key("sn", serial_number, slot=0)

There are 5 key slots, key0 to key4. Each is an indexed database column, so searches on keys are fast. Use the other slots for ids you will search on, such as a microcontroller unique id, a MAC address, or the serial number of a sub-assembly.

  • A key is stored as <name>:<value>, for example sn:A12345. Keep the whole string within 64 characters, the size of the database column. A longer key is not saved, add_key() returns False and logs an error.

  • Use the same slot for the same id in every script of a product, and in every stage, see Key Slot Plan below.

  • The serial number can be read from the DUT, scanned from a label (with input_textbox()), or created and programmed by the test. When the test creates it, also print or program it onto the unit, otherwise the result can’t be matched to the unit later.

Key Slot Plan¶

Most products have more than one test stage. A common plan is a Board Level Test (BLT) of the PCBA, and a Final Assembly Test (FAT) of the assembled product, see Planning Your Test Stages. Use each key slot for the same id in every stage. For example, when the microcontroller unique id identifies the unit, BLT saves it in key0, and FAT saves it in key0 too. One query on key0 then finds the BLT and FAT results of a unit, and the Lente yield chart counts the unit once.

Do the same across products. When every product uses key0 for the unit id and key1 for the MAC address, the same queries, reports and MES integration work for all of them.

Make a table of the key slot usage for all your products, or for each product family, before writing the scripts, and keep it with your scripts (for example in a README),

  • key0 is the unit id in every product and every stage, it must be known at the first stage. An id that is only known later, like a label printed at FAT, gets its own slot, left empty in the earlier stages.

  • Never use a slot for a different id in another stage or product, leave it empty instead. Reserve the last slots for product specific ids.

  • Use the same key name for the same id everywhere, for example always sn, not sn in one script and serial in another.

  • Put the table in your code as constants in a common module, used by every script,

    DBKEY_SERIAL_NUM = 0
DBKEY_MAC = 1
DBKEY_LABEL_SN = 2

ctx.record.add_key("sn", mcu_uid, slot=DBKEY_SERIAL_NUM)

Firmware and Hardware Versions¶

Record versions read from the DUT as string measurements. A string measurement always passes, and is stored with the test item,

success, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("fw_ver", fw_ver, ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING)

  • Record the version the DUT reports, after programming, not only the file that was programmed.

  • Record the bootloader, application and any co-processor versions separately.

  • A hardware revision that the test writes to the DUT (for example from a select sub) should also be recorded as a measurement.

  • String values are stored in a 128 character column.

Test Equipment¶

To trace a fault to a jig or instrument, record the serial number of each piece of test equipment as a string measurement in the setup item. For example the scope, power supply and programmer serial numbers, and the jig controller’s id. A unit tested on an instrument later found out of calibration can then be found in the results.

A string measurement has no limits, it always passes and is only recorded. Drivers often return a unique_id from discover_channels() for this,

drivers = self.shared_state.get_drivers(self.chan, type="AGILENT_DSO_USB_1")
dso_sn = drivers[0]["obj"]["unique_id"]
success, _result, _bullet = ctx.record.measurement("dso_sn", dso_sn, ResultAPI.UNIT_STRING)

  • Record every instrument the test uses, including shared ones, in every result.

  • For a shared instrument with several inputs, also record the input used by the channel.

  • Use the same measurement name for the same instrument in all your scripts, so one query finds them all.

  • If a driver does not give a unique_id, read the serial number from the instrument, for example its *IDN? reply.

Lots¶

info_lot (16 characters) is the lot or work order. It usually comes from a sub, so the operator enters it or a Traveller sets it. Use a regex on the sub to enforce your lot format, see subs. The Lente Throughput & Yield chart can group results by lot.

Test Versions¶

The script records which test ran (meta_script), and the scripts version records the exact files. Decide how a change shows up in your searches,

  • Changing a limit or a test item in place keeps the script name. Searches by meta_script then mix results from both versions. Use meta_git_public or the date to separate them.

  • Making a new script version (for example P00100_T0101_SmokeTests.scr) keeps the versions separate in every search. This is the better choice for changes made by an ECO.

  • Measurement names include the module and item names. Renaming either starts a new series in the database, which breaks trend charts and SQL queries across the change.

See Naming Proposal for a naming scheme that puts the stage and version in the names.

Example Queries¶

All results for one unit, in time order,

select r.id, r.info_product, r.meta_script, r.meta_result, r.meta_start, r.meta_git_public
from record r
where r.key0 = 'sn:A12345'
order by r.meta_start

The firmware version recorded for each unit of a lot,

select r.key0, m.value, r.meta_start
from measurement m join record r on m.record_id = r.id
where m.name = 'mycompany.P001.P00100_T0100_SmokeTests.TST0100_connect.fw_ver'
      and r.info_lot = 'L2026-07'
order by r.meta_start

See SQL Queries for more queries and tools.

Checklist¶

Before production, decide,

  1. which id identifies a unit (key0), and where it comes from

  2. which other ids are keys, and their slot numbers, in a key slot table shared by all your products or product family, see Key Slot Plan

  3. which versions are recorded (firmware, bootloader, hardware revision)

  4. which test equipment serial numbers are recorded, and their measurement names

  5. the lot format, and who enters it (operator, Traveller)

  6. how scripts and test items are named and versioned

  7. how long results are kept, and where (Lente, upstream Lente, backups)
